All exhibits regardless of judging date must be in place by 7 p.m. on Wednesday of current exhibit year. 13 Step Three: Bring Your Entries to the Fair 1. Do not bring exhibits prior to 1 pm on Wednesday of current exhibit year. Fair officials are not responsible for exhibits brought in earlier than that time. All exhibits must be brought to the appropriate building or conference judging area on Wednesday of current exhibit year between 1 pm and 7 pm. The following are exceptions to this requirement: a. Junior, Open and Senior citizen flowers and house plants (Dept. 15J, 15 and 150) must be in place by 6 pm on Wednesday of current exhibit year. b. Dairy and llamas must be unloaded and stalled by noon on Thursday of current exhibit year. These animals may be brought in on Wednesday if desired. c. Hogs must be unloaded and in pens by 6 pm on Wednesday of current exhibit year. 2. Report to the Superintendent of Entries in the Administrative Building to pick up your exhibit tags and for directions to the appropriate exhibit building. 3. Check tags for errors. Only the Superintendent of Entries may alter tags and judges sheets. 4. You will receive a wristband with your entry tags. This wristband is your season pass and must be worn for entry into the fair park on subsequent days. Exhibitors who cannot wear the wristband because of health issues or work/employment regulations must obtain an alternative pass from the Fair Secretary. 5. Wristbands must be placed on the exhibitor’s wrist securely. 6. Junior exhibitors need to check the judging schedule to assure they are present for face-to-face and/or conference judging of exhibits. 7. Exhibitors submitting entries and then not exhibiting or attending the fair shall forfeit all stall and cage fees as well as the cost of the exhibitor gate admission ticket. Exhibitors attending the fair may still pick up their exhibitor season pass. Step Four: Exhibiting and Judging 1. Attach your exhibit tag to your entry and save the bottom portion (claim ticket) for use on the final fair day to pick up your exhibit. 2. Bring the exhibit to the designated exhibit building. 3. Open and Senior Citizen Division exhibitors do not need to be present for judging. Exhibits must be in place by 7 pm on Wednesday of current exhibit year. Open and Senior class flower entries must be in by 6 pm. 4. Junior Division Exhibitors—all of your exhibits must be in place by 7 pm on Wednesday of current exhibit year even if you must return on another day for face-to-face judging. 5. Report to the judging area with your exhibit on the day and time designated for face-to-face judging. You will be directed on what to do with your exhibit after judging is completed. 6. Animals must be in the show ring promptly after being called. Any exhibitor failing to comply will be excluded from competing. No one, except exhibitors of animals, judges, and fair officials will be allowed inside a show ring during the exhibition. 7. No pets or other animals are allowed at the fair park unless they are part of an exhibit or are a service animal. 8. Exhibits are to be entered in the name of the owner. Junior division exhibitors may enter and show managerial animals provided a managerial agreement between the owner and exhibitor has been approved and discussed. 9. No selling of animals (except quality meat animals) allowed until after 4:30 pm on Sunday of current exhibit year. 10. All exhibits must remain at the fair park until 4:30 pm on Sunday of current exhibit year. Any exhibitor removing exhibits prior to this time will forfeit premiums. The only exception is if a fair official or the veterinarian orders/allows animals to be removed for health or safety reasons. 11. You must care for your exhibit during the fair. Failure to feed and water animals and to maintain clean pens/stalls may result in forfeiture of all premiums. 12. Premiums checks will be distributed in October or November. Please cash them promptly. In the event State Aid for premiums in not received, reduced premiums may be paid to exhibitors. Overnight Barn Passes Overnight barn permits will be limited. Youth interested in staying in the barns must register with their leader or advisor prior to the fair. Animal numbers will be utilized in determining the number of youth awarded overnight barn passes. Any changes during the fair must be approved by the Extension Office. Barn permits are issued by the Extension Office and must be picked up by the exhibitor prior to 5:00 pm of the day that the permit is to be used. No open class exhibitors can stay in the barns overnight. 14 Judges and Types of Judging Judges will be selected from outside Polk County as is feasible. Every effort will be made to engage the most qualified judges. Open and Senior Citizen Divisions: Regular judging and placing is followed for these divisions. This procedure is one first place, one second place, one third place and one fourth place regardless of the number of entries in each lot number. Judges are not required to award a placing(s) if none of the exhibits warrant the placing. Junior Division: Face-to-face judging procedure is used in many departments as this is an educational focused fair. The exhibitor brings the exhibit to the judge; the judge discusses the exhibit with the exhibitor; and then the judge places the exhibit in the appropriate award group according to or comparing it to a standard of perfection or the ideal. The Danish judging system is used for all other junior exhibits. This is described in detail in ATCP 160.92(3) (a). The awards for each placing are based on the number of entries in the lot. Judges may award more blue or red ribbons than allowed but the premiums must be paid according to the Danish system. In lots with only one exhibitor, judges are not required to award a placing if the exhibit does not warrant the placing. Judges are instructed in cases of attempted interference on the part of exhibitors or members of their families with the judges’ deliberations and decisions, to exclude parties so offending from competition in the particular lot number. All protests against awards made must be in writing and signed by the party deeming him/herself aggrieved. A protest must be delivered to the Fair Secretary within 2 days after the award was made. A protest shall include specifications of charges and/or grounds of complaint and the name(s), address (es), and phone numbers(s) of witness (es). The Fair Secretary shall present the protest to the Board of Directors for review, discussion and decision. General requirements for event organizers All fairs or exhibitions of any length must obtain, review, and keep for five years all required records and test results: • Exhibitor’s name and address • Animal identification (number, type, description, and, when required, official identification (see requirements for different animals below)) • Documents showing compliance with disease testing and other health requirements • Livestock premises number, if any, where animals originated • Documentation showing legal importation to the event (if applicable) and, when required, movement to the event (see requirements for different animals below) • For swine, a record of any swine transported directly to a slaughtering establishment • For swine, a record of any swine transported to an animal market where all animals sold at the market sale for that day were shipped directly to a slaughtering establishment Fairs or exhibitions lasting more than 24 hours must appoint a licensed veterinarian to inspect all animals daily. Their conduct in this competitive environment shall always reflect the highest standards of honor and dignity to promote the advancement of agricultural education. This code applies to junior as well as open class exhibitors who compete in structured classes of competition. By entering an animal for exhibition at the Polk County Fair, the exhibitor consents to abide by the following guidelines: 1. All exhibitors must present, upon request of fair and livestock show officials, proof of ownership, managerial agreement, length of ownership and age of all animals entered. Misrepresentation of ownership, age, or any facts relating thereto is prohibited. 2. Owners and exhibitors shall provide animal health certificates from licensed veterinarians as required by the Animal Health Rules and Regulations of the Polk County Fair. 3. Junior exhibitors are expected to care for and groom their animals while at the Polk County Fair. The clipping and grooming of animals while on the fairgrounds is to be done by the exhibitor and can be assisted by immediate family members, including Polk County 4-H Leaders, FFA advisors or owners 4. Animals shall be presented to show events where they will enter the food chain free of drugs. The act of entering an animal in a livestock show is the giving of consent by the owner, exhibitor, for show management to obtain any specimens of urine, saliva, blood, or other substances from the animal to be used in testing. 5. Any surgical procedure or injection of any foreign substance or drug which could affect the animals’ performance or alter its natural contour, confirmation, or appearance, is prohibited. Exceptions will be made for external applications of substances to the hoofs or horns of animals which affect appearance only and for surgical procedures performed by a duly licensed veterinarian for the sole purpose of protecting the health of the animal. 6. The use of showing and/or handling practices or devices such as striking animals to cause swelling, using electrical contrivance, or other similar practices are not acceptable and are prohibited. 7. Direct criticism or interference with the judge, fair or livestock show management, other exhibitors, or show officials before, during, or after the competitive event is prohibited. In the furtherance of their official duty, all judges, fair and livestock show management, or other show officials shall be treated with courtesy, cooperation and respect and no person shall direct abusive or threatening conduct toward them. 8. No owner, exhibitor, shall conspire with another person or persons to intentionally violate this code of ethics. 9. The act of entering of an animal in the Polk County Fair implies that the owner, exhibitor, has read this Code of Ethics and agrees to abide by these provisions. 10. No Quality Meats animal can be moved from the appropriate exhibit barn and housed in a different location during the fair. Muffins, Plain 2 cups flour 2 teaspoons baking powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 2 tablespoons sugar 1 cup milk 1/4 cup melted butter 1 egg, beaten Combine flour, baking powder, salt and sugar in medium bowl. Mix well. In a large measuring cup, measure milk. Add butter. Add egg and beat with a fork. Add to dry ingredients. Stir only until well moistened. Spoon dough into the greased muffin tins, filling two-thirds full. Bake at 400 degrees for 20 to 25 minutes. Serve hot with butter. This recipe makes 12 muffins. 137 2. Cookies, Chocolate Chip 1/3 cup shortening 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour 1/3 cup butter or margarine, softened 1/2 teaspoon soda 1/2 cup granulated sugar 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 cup brown sugar (packed) 1 package (6 ounces) semi-sweet chocolate pieces 1 egg 1 teaspoon vanilla Pre-heat your oven to 375 degrees. In a large bowl, cream together shortening, butter, sugars, egg and vanilla. Stir in flour, soda and salt. Mix in chocolate chips. Drop by teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet. Bake about 8-10 minutes or until light brown. 5. Mix butter, sugar, egg yolks and flavoring thoroughly. Measure and work in flour. Using one-fourth at a time, force dough through cookie press onto ungreased baking sheet in desired shapes. Bake 7 to 10 minutes, or until set but not brown. This recipe makes about 6 dozen cookies. 7. Cookies, Sugar 1 cup butter or margarine 4 1/4 cups flour 1 cup cooking oil 1 teaspoon salt 1 cup white sugar 1 teaspoon soda 1 cup powdered sugar 1 teaspoon cream of tartar 2 eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Beat first four ingredients very well with an electric mixer. Add one egg at a time and beat well after each. Add flour and other ingredients. Mix well. Make balls the size of a walnut and roll in white sugar. Press lightly on cookie sheet with glass dipped in sugar. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes or until edges are slightly brown. 138 8. Unfold and ease pastry loosely into pan, being careful not to stretch. Stretching causes pastry to shrink during baking. Trim pastry with scissors 1/2" from edge of pan. Fold pastry under, even with pan. Form a fluted edge by firmly placing the right index finger on the inside of rim, left thumb and index finger on outside of pastry at that point. Pinch. Repeat all around pie. Sharpen points by pinching each one firmly. Hook points under pan rim to help prevent shrinking during baking. Prick pie shell. Bake at 475 degrees 8 to 10 minutes. Cool. Fill with cream or chiffon-type filling or other refrigerated fillings. Finish according to recipe. 19. Single Pastry Shell, 2 variations (Easy Flaky Pie Crust) 3 cups flour 1 ½ cups shortening ½ teaspoon salt 5 tablespoons cool water 1 tablespoon vinegar 1 egg Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Combine flour, shortening and salt, mix well. In another bowl, mix together water, vinegar and egg. Combine mixtures and mix lightly with fork. Roll out and put in pie pan. Bake at 425 degrees for 10-12 minutes. NOTE: This can be rolled out several times and still comes out tender and flaky. Yield: 4 single pie crusts or 2 double. Who Shows - Children ages 5-9, who have worked with the animal prior to the Fair. How Is It Set Up? • Children need to have a parent/guardian or older youth in the ring when the child and animal are in the ring. • The animal needs to be shown with a halter (rope or leather); adult may assist. • The animals are the youngest class of animals allowed in the species: • Beef and dairy cattle – junior calf; sheep – young lamb; goats – kid (youngest class) • The animals will be brought the day of the show and taken home the same day. There will be a designated area for the Little Britches animals on Sunday morning. Animals may be used from youth exhibitors already showing at the Fair and they are housed with their 4-H/FFA chapter. • The “judge” has the child and animal circle in the ring (child has the option of posing the animal or not) and then the judge will ask each exhibitor questions related to the animal. • Each child is given a participation ribbon from the Polk County Fair Society and a coupon for a root beer float from the Polk Burnett Dairy Producers. Each child will pick up their name tag, to be placed on their front side - so judges can call them by name when they check in. The youth will bring their animal into the ring, the judge will speak to them, Fairest of the Fair royalty will give them their ribbon and root beer coupon, then they will be asked to stand in front of the Little Britches backdrop to get their picture taken. The Polk County Agriculture Advocates will then take their photo and have it printed and back in the barn by 1pm for families to pick up. Photos are posted on the Little Britches photo backdrop. • All animals must have a permanent ID tag upon entering the fairgrounds and be in good health according to the fair book health guidelines for the species. All animals must have the required tags prior to the show - as designated by species in the health requirements.
